name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Jim Baird running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger Drew Cox raised only ~$20K
model.rationale: The R+15 district, Baird's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage over a barely funded challenger leave little room for competition, and markets agree at roughly 94% Republican. No polls or expert ratings suggest movement, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based baseline.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Cox or a scandal involving Baird would be the only realistic path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Baird seeks another term in a west-central Indiana district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. He enters the general election after easily securing renomination, with roughly $92,000 on hand and more than half a million dollars in outside support, though some outside groups have spent against him. Democrat Drew Cox has raised only about $20,000, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Baird about a 94% chance of winning. With such a large partisan lean and financial gap, the seat remains firmly in Republican hands barring an unexpected development.
